title: Winter SOI gave no clear added next-winter Nino 3.4 forecast gain at 1981-2024 origins
abstract: We tested whether winter air pressure adds next-winter Nino 3.4 forecast value beyond current temperature, its change since autumn and different warm and cold slopes. Earlier-year fits used fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 and standardized SOI snapshots. At 44 origins in 1981-2024, adding winter SOI raised mean squared error by 2.74%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -7.58% to +1.09%. RMSE rose from 1.0751 to 1.0897 C. All planned checks also gave intervals that include zero, including a spatial temperature contrast control. This extends earlier short-lead and spring pressure tests to a winter-to-winter benchmark. It does not show that atmospheric information has no value. Revised data, simple models, few winters and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate loss records, draws, numerical checks and a figure are included. Raw source data remain external.

display.caption: Added winter SOI gave uncertain MSE changes. Lines give conditional 95% five-year block limits. Positive reduction means lower error.
